ambiguities.evidence: Equation (3.4a) divides by ||x||_infinity, while the surrounding section quantifies over a row x without excluding x=0 [PDF p. 5, printed B789, section 3.1 and eq. (3.4a)].
ambiguities.impact: A formal translation must either assume x is nonzero or add a separate zero-row convention; neither choice is stated by the paper.
ambiguities.issue: Zero rows are not handled explicitly.

ambiguities.evidence: The paragraph before (3.2) describes a maximum coefficient in (theta/2,theta], whereas (3.4a) uses ||x||_infinity [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph before eq. (3.2) and eq. (3.4a)].
ambiguities.impact: The mathematically coherent reading is maximum absolute magnitude, but that interpretation comes from the norm formula rather than an explicit prose definition.
ambiguities.issue: The prose says 'maximum coefficient,' while the formula uses an infinity norm.

contract_plain_english: For each nonzero row x, choose its positive power-of-two scale lambda so that the largest absolute entry of lambda x is greater than theta/2 and at most theta; equivalently theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity, with theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)) [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.2) and (3.4a)].

source_evidence.observation: The input format has unit roundoff u, normalized range +/-[f_min,f_max], and underflow-error envelope g_min; equation (2.3) models input rounding, assuming no overflow, by fl(z)=z(1+delta)+eta with |delta|<=u, |eta|<=g_min, and eta*delta=0.

Accumulation-format operations use unit roundoff U and underflow envelope G_min. The default models use round-to-nearest; directed rounding is covered only after replacing u,g_min,U,G_min by twice their values.

The matrix algorithm is Lambda^{-1}(fl(Lambda A)fl(BM))M^{-1}. Lambda and M are nonsingular diagonal matrices, and their scaling factors are powers of two so that scaling introduces no rounding error.

A, B, and C are assumed exactly representable in sufficiently high precision outside the scaled MMA computation. The maximum magnitude on each scaled row of Lambda A and each scaled column of BM is placed in (theta/2,theta], where theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)).

For an inner product x^T y, the scaled expression is lambda^{-1}mu^{-1}fl(lambda x)^T fl(mu y). The row factor satisfies theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity; the column factor has the analogous inequality with y and mu.

After scaling, conversion to the input format can incur either relative rounding error or absolute underflow error componentwise; these later errors are separate from the exact scaling-factor interval in (3.4a).

statement.algorithm_linkage: Equation (3.4a) chooses the row factor used in s=lambda^{-1}mu^{-1}fl(lambda x)^T fl(mu y), itself the inner-product specialization of the matrix scaling algorithm (3.1) [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, eqs. (3.1), (3.3), and (3.4a)].
binders: A in R^(m x n), B in R^(n x q), and C=AB are the matrices in the section-3 matrix product [PDF p. 4, printed B788, section 3 and eq. (3.1)].
x in R^n is a row of A and lambda is its corresponding diagonal entry of Lambda [PDF p. 5, printed B789, section 3.1 before eq. (3.3)].
n is the inner-product length, and theta=min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)) [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.2)].
conclusions: The exact row-scaling constraint is theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].

Equivalently for a positive lambda, theta/2<lambda||x||_infinity<=theta, so the maximum magnitude of the scaled row lambda x lies in the half-open interval (theta/2,theta] [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph before eq. (3.2) and eq. (3.4a)].
constants_and_indexing: The lower endpoint has the exact factor 2 and is strict; the upper endpoint is non-strict [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].
lambda is row-specific, whereas mu is column-specific [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.3)-(3.4b)].
The square root in theta is sqrt(F_max/n), not F_max/n [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.2)].
definitions_and_conventions: theta is the largest proposed common scale ceiling that respects both input overflow, theta<=f_max, and accumulation overflow, theta<=sqrt(F_max/n) [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph and eq. (3.2)].
fl denotes rounding to the input format [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, eq. (2.3) and its following explanation].
The analogous column factor is theta/(2||y||_infinity)<mu<=theta/||y||_infinity [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4b)].
error_notions: Equation (3.4a) is a scaling-factor bound, not a forward-error or rounding-error inequality [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].
Subsequent componentwise conversion errors satisfy |Delta x|<=u lambda|x|+g_min [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.5)].
exceptional_values: The formula is undefined for a zero row because ||x||_infinity appears in the denominator, and the nearby text gives no zero-row convention [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].
Overflow is to be prevented by theta, while input underflow after scaling remains allowed and is modeled in (3.5) [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.2) and (3.5)].
The analysis takes A and B to be real matrices and does not formulate the claim for NaNs or infinities [PDF p. 4, printed B788, opening of section 3].
higher_order_terms: No asymptotic, omitted, or higher-order term occurs in equation (3.4a); it is an exact interval constraint [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].
hypotheses: The computation uses the mixed-precision MMA setting of Model 1, with input and accumulation formats as specified there [PDF pp. 2-3, printed B786-B787, Model 1 and eqs. (2.1)-(2.4)].
Lambda is nonsingular diagonal and lambda is a power of two, so the row scaling is intended to be exact [PDF p. 4, printed B788, text following eq. (3.1)].

The section assumes no underflow or overflow before scaling by Lambda and M or after unscaling, with A, B, and C stored exactly in sufficiently high precision [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, paragraph spanning the page break after eq. (3.1)].
The displayed formula implicitly requires ||x||_infinity>0; the paper does not separately state this nonzero-row condition [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].
implicit_context: The interval is a rowwise instance of the diagonal scaling in (3.1), not a standalone claim about arbitrary lambda [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, eqs. (3.1)-(3.4a)].

The preceding prose says the maximum magnitude of every scaled row and column is selected in (theta/2,theta], supplying the intended maximal power-of-two choice [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding eq. (3.2)].
norms: The formula uses the vector infinity norm ||x||_infinity; the surrounding prose identifies lambda||x||_infinity with the maximum scaled-row magnitude, although no standalone norm definition is given there [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph before eq. (3.2) and eq. (3.4a)].
numerical_model: The input format has precision t, u=2^(-t), normalized range +/-[f_min,f_max], and g_min=f_min/2 without subnormals or u f_min with gradual underflow [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1 and eq. (2.1)].

The accumulation format has T>=t, U=2^(-T), exponent range containing the input range, and G_min=F_min/2 without subnormals or U F_min with gradual underflow [PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1 and eq. (2.2)].
The scaling interval itself is exact; rounding and underflow enter only when fl(lambda x) is formed [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eqs. (3.4a)-(3.6)].

undebatable_constraints: Preserve theta/(2||x||_infinity)<lambda<=theta/||x||_infinity exactly, including endpoint strictness [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.4a)].
lambda must be the power-of-two diagonal factor associated with row x [PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, text after eq. (3.1) and eq. (3.3)].
theta must be min(f_max,sqrt(F_max/n)) [PDF p. 5, printed B789, eq. (3.2)].
The conclusion concerns the scaled-row maximum and must not be recast as a rounding-error theorem [PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph before eq. (3.2) and eq. (3.4a)].
